newsitem.title: UK: Dip in U.S. Treasuries spills into Bradys.
newsitem.headline: Dip in U.S. Treasuries spills into Bradys.

text.p: Weaker U.S. Treasureis took their toll on emerging debt prices at mid-morning on Tuesday but initially, any drops were small.
"We need a bit of a correction after the run-up in the past two weeks," a European bank trader said.
Activity was subdued after the U.S. holiday on Monday and before Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony later in the day.
A number of prices were off early highs, including Russia, which at one stage was bid over 80 cents in the dollar for Vneshekonombank dollar paper RUVNUSLNS=RR, the first time in about two months.
It later slipped back to a bid of 79-1/2 cents.
Russian debt, already a market favourite, has been helped up this week by the apparent recovery of President Boris Yeltsin from pneumonia.
However, the debt is still subject to rumours about the state of his health, which one trader said may have been responsible for the the mid-morning correction.
The most recent Kremlin statement said he was recovering at a government residence outside Moscow where he was working on state papers but had no meetings planned.
Exotics have been one of the biggest beneficiaries of recent price gains as investors searched further to pick up high yield debt.
Morocco has stood out, with some strong buying at the end of last week, notably by two major U.S. banks, propelling the price for Series A MOFLA09=RR more than a point higher.
It has since levelled off near 85-5/8 cents in the dollar.

The rise was also partly attributed to a widening gap with Argentine FRBs, a link many in the market continue to watch even though there are few obvious fundamental similarities betwen the two economies.
There is also talk of a possible rating for Morocco and a new bond issue this year.

Algerian debt investors ignored growing violence in the country, and traders said they were still expecting relatively high oil prices, which would allow the country to comfortably meet debt repayments.
